Thus, as a finite-Levi module, S_n has weights only zero or finite-sl3 roots.

A highest weight among zero or the six roots is dominant only for zero or the highest root, giving the trivial representation or the adjoint representation respectively. The literal Chevalley brackets and both sets of original Serre relations hold: the three cyclic off-diagonal matrix units have the required h-weights and mixed brackets, and the double adjoint of one cyclic unit on either other unit vanishes; similarly for the opposite units. Thus universality gives an actual Lie homomorphism pi:g_S(A(1,1))->sl3 tensor C[t,t^(-1)]. It is not assumed faithful.

The image of S_n is contained in sl3 tensor t^n, and pi is sl3-equivariant. To prove its adjoint restriction is nonzero for EVERY n, set h=[e1,[e2,e3]], of degree (1,1,1). Matrix-unit multiplication gives pi(h)=(E11-E22) tensor t and [(E11-E22),E31]=-E31. Therefore pi((ad h)^(n-1)e3)=(-1)^(n-1) E31 tensor t^n, a nonzero symbolic formula for every n>=1. The unique adjoint summand maps isomorphically onto sl3 tensor t^n, while pi kills every trivial Z_n because the adjoint module has no sl3-invariant vector. Consequently ker(pi|S_n)=Z_n.
trace_cocycle_induction: Base n=1: S_1 is the actual adjoint V, so Z_1=0. Inductively assume Z_j=0 for every 1<=j<n. For each such j let A_j be the UNIQUE element of S_j mapping to A tensor t^j. Complete reducibility also gives a unique equivariant adjoint section A_n of pi at level n, with S_n={A_n:A in sl3} direct-sum Z_n.

For positive i,j with i+j=n, equivariance and pi([A_i,B_j])=[A,B] tensor t^n give [A_i,B_j]=[A,B]_n+Tr(AB)c_(i,j) for a uniquely determined c_(i,j) in Z_n. The reason is that the only sl3-invariant bilinear tensor on the two adjoint modules is a scalar multiple of Tr(AB), by Schur's lemma and the nondegenerate finite-Levi trace pairing. Bracket skew-symmetry gives c_(j,i)=-c_(i,j), in particular c_(i,i)=0. This is a purely algebraic trace tensor; no positive form is assumed.

For positive i,j,k with i+j+k=n, all three INNER brackets have level below n, so the induction hypothesis makes them exactly [A,B]_(i+j), etc. Project Jacobi for A_i,B_j,C_k to Z_n. Cyclicity of the trace makes Tr([A,B]C)=Tr([B,C]A)=Tr([C,A]B); choose A,B,C with this trilinear expression nonzero, or equivalently use its nonzero invariant tensor. The result is c_(i+j,k)+c_(j+k,i)+c_(k+i,j)=0, equivalently c_(i+j,k)=c_(i,j+k)+c_(j,k+i). No assumption that Z_n is central in the full algebra is made.

Fix n and set t_a=c_(a,n-a) for 1<=a<=n-1. When n=2, t_1=0 by skew-symmetry. When n>=3, choosing i=1,j=a-1,k=n-a gives t_a=t_1+t_(a-1) for 2<=a<=n-1. Thus t_a=a t_1. Skew-symmetry also gives t_(n-1)=-t_1, so n t_1=0. Characteristic zero implies all c_(i,j)=0. This is a uniform symbolic induction, not a finite root enumeration or selected parameter calculation.

Because Splus is generated by S_1=V, every level n>=2 is spanned by brackets [S_i,S_(n-i)] with 1<=i<n. With every c_(i,n-i)=0 these brackets lie in the adjoint section and have no Z_n component. Therefore Z_n=0. Induction proves pi|S_n is an isomorphism for every n>=1.
